documentation_gaps.title: Reconciler behavior and alerting during payment processor outages is undocumented
documentation_gaps.description: The documentation describes a nightly Reconciler Job that depends on the external payment processor’s reporting API to produce discrepancy summaries, but does not state what happens when that API is unavailable or degraded at run time. It is unknown whether the job retries, uses backoff or alternate scheduling, supports catch-up runs, or raises alerts when it cannot retrieve a complete settlement report. This prevents assessing how long reconciliation may be delayed and whether operators or finance analysts are notified when the nightly run fails or is incomplete.
documentation_gaps.importance: Understanding the Reconciler’s failure-handling, retry, and alerting behavior during payment processor outages is necessary to evaluate the real availability impact of this threat: whether a missed run simply delays reconciliation by one day, whether it self-heals via retries or catch-up runs, or whether failures could go unnoticed without operator action.
requested_evidence: Documentation of the Reconciler Job’s retry and backoff strategy when calls to the payment processor reporting API fail or time out, including limits on retries and overall execution time.
Documentation of any catch-up mechanism for missed or failed nightly reconciliation runs (for example, re-running for prior days once the payment processor API is available again).

Documentation of monitoring and alerting for Reconciler Job failures or incomplete runs, including who is notified and through which channel when the nightly reconciliation does not complete successfully.

catalog_gap_candidates.concern: The catalog has no requirement that addresses resilience and operational handling for scheduled batch jobs that depend on external providers, such as documenting retry/backoff behavior, catch-up mechanisms, and alerting when an external reporting API is unavailable. In this system, the nightly Reconciler Job runs once per day and depends on the payment processor’s reporting API; an outage can delay reconciliation, but no existing requirement clearly asks that such dependencies be engineered and documented for availability and failure handling.

nearest_requirements.why_not: req-TPI-002 focuses on bounding work and cost when external events or retries trigger processing against metered services. The concern here is not unbounded consumption but the absence of documented resilience (retries, catch-up, alerting) for a scheduled batch job when its external dependency is unavailable.

req-OPS-002 is about detecting anomalous spend on metered infrastructure and routing those alerts, whereas this concern is about timely detection and handling of failed or incomplete batch reconciliations due to third-party outages, even when spend is normal.

req-OPS-005 governs how alerts are scoped and routed so they remain actionable once defined, but it does not require that critical batch jobs or external data-feed failures actually raise alerts or that their failure-handling behavior be documented.
